To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
every graph contains an independent set intersecting all maximum cliques.
every graph contains at least one cycle intersecting all its maximum independent sets.
every graph contains an independent set of maximum size and that every graph with maximum stability number is spanned by cycles of size at most the stability number.
In summary, our research is concerned with
cycle partitions in graphs.
the cycle partition problem, which asks for a set of cycles that covers all maximum independent sets of a graph.

the following problems: (1) Given an n-vertex graph G, find the smallest integer k such that G contains k disjoint cycles, (2) Given an n -vertex graph G with stability number α, find the smallest number of cycles that span G, (3) Given a graph G with stability numbers α and β, find the smallest α-β-vertex set that is a cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
every non-trivial graph contains at least two disjoint cycles.
every non-trivial graph contains a cycle partition of order α.
every graph with α maximum independent sets contains a cycle intersected by each of these α sets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a graph G is cycle partitionable if and only if it is stable.
we prove that every non-trivial graph contains a cycle partition of order at most α, and that every graph contains at most 2α−2 degenerate cycle partitions of order α.
every graph contains at most α + 1 degenerate cycles, which intersect all maximum independent sets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
every graph is spanned by cycles, and that every cycle in a graph intersects all maximum independent sets.
the structure of graphs with large stability number is closely related to the structure of their cycle partitions.
, in some sense, the structure of a graph is determined by the structure of its cycles.
